characterization_methods.key_findings: 6Al alloy tensile strength ~670-770 MPa and elongation to fracture ~30-55% (Fig. 4).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1
characterization_methods.purpose: Mechanical screening (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, total elongation)

characterization_methods.key_findings: Hardness nearly flat at ~200 HBW over 0-6Al (Fig. 3d).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm

characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in final materials; as-cast coarse dendritic microstructure; hot rolling plus water quenching gave fully recrystallized ~20 µm grain size with retained Mn microsegregations.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction; standard metallographic techniques

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five different alloys were synthesized in one operation using five movable Cu molds successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10×50×130 mm³-sized blocks were hot rolled at 1100 °C into 2±0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
Sheets were reheated to 1100 °C, water quenched, and cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine 2×60×55 mm³ segments for each alloy composition.
Aging was conducted in air at 550 °C for 1 h, followed by oil quenching (one of the nine RAP heat treatments).
Scales were removed from the surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized microstructure with a grain size of ~20 µm and some retained microsegregations of Mn (austenitic Fe-30Mn-1.2C-6Al matrix).

unmapped_findings: Alloys with Al additions of 4 wt.% and 6 wt.% are only very weakly affected by the applied aging treatments in terms of their mechanical data, compared with Fe-30Mn-1.2C (weakening/embrittlement) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening). [b0024]

The intermediate alloy variants with Al concentrations of 2–6 wt.% do not show equivalent mechanical properties compared to the ~8 wt.% Al variant, and a much smaller influence of aging on the tensile behavior is observed in the 2–6 wt.% Al cases. [b0025]
